seoTitle: How to Write Off an Outstanding Invoice in QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Write off an uncollectible invoice in QuickBooks Online with a Bad Debt expense account, a Bad Debt product item, and a credit memo applied through Receive Payment.
intro: Not every invoice gets paid. A customer closes their account, a debt goes stale, or collections simply aren't worth pursuing, and when that happens, leaving the invoice sitting open overstates your accounts receivable and skews your profit and loss. QuickBooks Online doesn't have a single "write off" button. It uses a credit memo tied to a dedicated Bad Debt item to zero out the balance while keeping a clean paper trail. This guide walks through that exact process, including the account and item setup QuickBooks requires before the credit memo will work.
prerequisites: An invoice you're certain is uncollectible
Permission to create new accounts and products/services in QuickBooks Online

steps.heading: Find the invoices worth writing off
steps.body: Log into QuickBooks Online and check the Business overview, where bank balances, profit and loss, and unpaid invoices are summarized on the dashboard. For a fuller picture, run Reports > Standard reports > Accounts Receivable Aging Detail, which lists every open invoice by how overdue it is. Before writing anything off, this report tells you whether you're dealing with one stray invoice or a pattern worth addressing with a customer directly.

image.caption: The QuickBooks Online homepage after login, with bank balances, profit and loss, and unpaid invoice totals summarized on one screen.

steps.heading: Create a Bad Debts expense account
steps.body: QuickBooks treats a write-off as a credit applied against an open invoice, not a deletion, which keeps the original sale on the books for your accountant and any audit trail. Before you can do that, go to Chart of accounts and select New. Set Account Type to Expenses and Detail Type to Bad debts, and name it "Bad debts". This is the account the write-off's cost lands in.

steps.heading: Create a Bad Debts product/service item
steps.body: Go to Products & services (under Sales, or Get Paid & Pay in some accounts) and select New > Non-inventory. Name it "Bad debts" and set its income account to the Bad debts expense account you just created, not a regular income account. Enable "I sell this product/service to my customers" so it's selectable on a credit memo. This item is what turns a credit memo into a genuine write-off instead of a discount or refund.

steps.heading: Create a credit memo for the invoice amount
steps.body: Start a new credit memo and select the customer tied to the outstanding invoice. In the line items, choose the Bad debts item and enter the amount, either the full remaining balance or a partial figure if you're only writing off part of it. QuickBooks' own instructions suggest adding "Bad Debt" in the message field for your records, since "why was this written off" is exactly the question you'll get asked later. Save the credit memo once the amount matches what you intend to forgive.

steps.heading: Apply the credit through Receive Payment
steps.body: Saving the credit memo creates an available credit on the customer's account, but it doesn't clear the invoice on its own. Open Receive payment, select the customer and the outstanding invoice, then select the credit memo from the Credits section before saving. Once applied, the invoice's remaining balance drops by the credited amount: a full write-off brings it to zero, and a partial one leaves the rest still owing.

image.caption: A saved credit memo with a single Bad Debt line item, subtotal, and tax calculated automatically. This is the credit applied through Receive Payment to zero out the invoice.

steps.heading: Confirm the write-off in your reports
steps.body: Head back to Sales, then Invoices, to confirm the change took effect: a written-off invoice should now show a reduced or zeroed balance instead of sitting in the unpaid column. Then check the Bad debts expense account in Chart of accounts, or run a Profit and Loss report, to see the write-off land as an expense for the period. This is the step people skip, and it's the one that confirms the write-off worked instead of just assuming the credit memo did its job.

image.caption: The Invoices list under Sales, showing unpaid and paid totals alongside each invoice's individual status after a credit has been applied.

troubleshooting.problem: The invoice still shows an open balance after saving the credit memo
troubleshooting.cause: A credit memo on its own doesn't touch the invoice. It has to be applied separately.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Receive payment, select the invoice, and select the credit memo from the Credits section before saving.

troubleshooting.problem: The write-off doesn't show up as an expense on the Profit and Loss report
troubleshooting.cause: The Bad debts product/service item's income account isn't pointed at the Bad debts expense account.
troubleshooting.fix: Edit the item so its income account is the dedicated Bad debts expense account, not a regular sales income account.

troubleshooting.problem: The Bad debts item doesn't appear as an option on the credit memo
troubleshooting.cause: The item was created without enabling "I sell this product/service to my customers".
troubleshooting.fix: Edit the product/service item and turn that setting on so it's selectable on sales forms.

faq.question: Does QuickBooks Online have a dedicated "write off invoice" button?
faq.answer: No. The method is a Bad Debts expense account plus a Bad Debts product/service item, used on a credit memo that's then applied against the open invoice through Receive payment.

faq.question: Will writing off an invoice delete the original sale from my records?
faq.answer: No, and that's the point. The invoice stays on record, and the credit memo offsets it, so you keep an audit trail showing both the original sale and the write-off.

faq.question: Can I write off only part of an invoice?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter the partial amount on the credit memo instead of the full balance, and apply it. The invoice will show a smaller remaining balance instead of being fully cleared.

faq.question: What account does the Bad Debts item need to be linked to?
faq.answer: A dedicated Expenses account with the Bad debts detail type, set as the item's income account, so the write-off lands on the correct line of your profit and loss.

faq.question: Does a write-off affect my profit and loss report?
faq.answer: Yes. The Bad Debts expense from the credit memo reduces net income for the period, which is why it should be reserved for genuinely uncollectible invoices instead of used casually.
